question.text:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows:

\[ \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \frac{1}{a_{nn}} \end{bmatrix} \]

In our case, we obtain

\[ A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{2}{3} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 &2 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows:

\[ \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \frac{1}{a_{nn}} \end{bmatrix} \]

In our case, we obtain

\[ A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{2}{3} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -4& 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} \sqrt{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows:

\[ \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \frac{1}{a_{nn}} \end{bmatrix} \]

In our case, we obtain

\[ A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \sqrt{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{3} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows:

\[ \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \frac{1}{a_{nn}} \end{bmatrix} \]

In our case, we obtain

\[ A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{4} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 &\frac{1}{4} \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Notice that the given matrix is diagonal.

The inverse of a diagonal matrix can be found as follows:

\[ \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \frac{1}{a_{nn}} \end{bmatrix} \]

In our case, we obtain

\[ A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 &\frac{1}{4} \end{bmatrix}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 &0\\ 0 & -\sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 &4 \end{bmatrix}. \]
